items.title: Equation of State for an Ideal Gas

source_refs.note: Equation of State for an Ideal Gas: a main subheading of 6.1 Assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 119-119.

blocks.text: A gas that obeys kinetic theory of gases is termed as an ideal gas. Ideal gas equation is given by
Here P represents pressure, V is volume, n is number of moles of the gas, R is universal gas constant (R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) and T is the temperature.
Equation (6.1) implies that product of pressure and volume is directly proportional to the temperature for an ideal gas.
